item.title: Trent McDuffie proved worth in win over Packers
item.description: The defense led the Los Angeles Rams to a victory over the Green Bay Packers on Wednesday night. Chris Shula’s unit forced three takeaways and allowed just 13 points to an opposing offense that can put up points in a hurry. One of the stronger individual performers? Trent McDuffie, one of LA’s prized offseason acquisitions. SumerSports charted 26 passing plays where McDuffie was matched up directly with a Packers receiver. You can’t realistically expect nor ask for better results. 11 plays vs Matthew Golden: 2 targets, 0 catches allowed 6 plays vs Christian Watson: 0 targets, 0 catches allowed 4 plays vs Tucker Kraft: 1 target, 0 catches allowed 3 plays vs Savion Williams: 1 target, 0 catches allowed 2 plays vs Bo Melton: 1 target, 1 catch for 12 yards While the Rams overall had trouble slowing down Watson, who accumulated four first-half receptions for 65 yards and a score before missing the second half due to injury, McDuffie was one of the defenders able to slow down his momentum. Kraft is one of the NFL’s top tight ends and the Rams held him to just three catches for 24 yards. Nate Landman punched out a fumble shortly after one of those receptions for a key defensive takeaway. All-in-all, Jordan Love finished with just 17 completions on 29 passes (59%) for 198 yards, one touchdown, two interceptions, and a passer rating of 62.1. This was an impressive outing for the Los Angeles defense. They limited Love and company even without the team’s other high-profile offseason addition at cornerback, Jaylen Watson. Emmanuel Forbes and Josh Wallace were also stingy in coverage, and that is a positive sign for the remainder of the season. Watson will not return in 2026. Even more positive is the fact the Packers had very little production on the ground. Savion Williams was the most efficient with two carries for 18 yards. Kaleb Johnson was held to 13 yards on eight carries (1.6 average). Byron Young and Myles Garrett each made notable tackles for loss that put Green Bay behind the chains. The Rams have now won five-straight games. Their previous four wins were against weaker competition. The defense is demonstrating they can get the job done even when facing superior quarterback talents and overall stronger opponents. Whether that is true for the offense remains to be seen. What is obvious is that the Rams are a defensive-led team in their current state. On Wednesday, Trent McDuffie proved his worth to a defense that is performing at a high level.

item.title: How Arsenal can expose Man City’s clear weakness to tighten grip on title
item.description: For Manchester City , life after three Champions League-winning midfielders began in earnest against Arsenal in August. They were a goal down after 23 seconds. It was an inauspicious start for Enzo Maresca and Elliot Anderson alike. A reunion with Arsenal on Sunday could be deemed a meeting of managerial midfielders, in Maresca and Mikel Arteta . Each learned from Pep Guardiola , who won the European Cup as a Barcelona player and manager and then in charge of City. But it is also a first Premier League clash since Bernardo Silva and Rodri joined their mentor in decamping from the Etihad Stadium in the summer. Arsenal may not have been sorry to see any go; if Guardiola’s resignation could facilitate an era of dominance from Arteta, and if it may have already begun with last season’s Premier League title, a further factor could be the departures of the City captain and Spain’s World Cup-winning skipper. If City have been confronted with the question of how to replace the irreplaceable, there are different answers. One is simply that it is impossible: they are irreplaceable. Another is: expensively. City committed £326m to three midfield recruits, in Anderson, Ayyoub Bouaddi and Enzo Fernandez . A third is: incoherently, at least so far. Perhaps it is unfair to expect newcomers, both in the dugout and the centre of the pitch, to bring the same cohesion and chemistry as predecessors who became the faces of longevity and continuity, but thus far they have not. A further subplot, arguably, is that Arsenal boast men who represented an alternative line of succession at City: not merely Arteta, Guardiola’s first assistant in Manchester, but Bruno Guimaraes , who was of interest at the Etihad in 2024, but when City chose not to activate his release clause, and Declan Rice , the target who preferred to join Arsenal in 2023. Arguably the England vice-captain was the best central midfielder in the Premier League even with Rodri and Silva; without them, and despite Pascal Gross’ extraordinary start to the season, he definitely is. Arsenal's Declan Rice and Bruno Guimaraes provide a key advantage over Man City in Bernardo Silva and Rodri's absence (Reuters) But if Arsenal won the war last season, City prevailed in the battles, based around the formidable double act of Silva and Rodri. They faced the Gunners three times; but for Gabriel Martinelli’s injury-time equaliser at the Emirates Stadium, they would have won all three. Rodri’s prowess then may have come at a cost: it was his third start in a week, and he only began two more games in the next three months. City had barely a third of the ball, in an anti-Pep performance, but were superb out of possession. In March’s Carabao Cup final, Nico O’Reilly’s box-crashing brace earned him the man-of-the-match award, but victory was underpinned by the midfield platform constructed by the Portuguese and the Spaniard. item.title: Adeyemi, Gavi react after Sabah 1-4 Barcelona: ‘We want to win every match’
item.description: Adeyemi, Gavi react after Sabah 1-4 Barcelona: ‘We want to win every match’ Karim Adeyemi continued his impressive UEFA Champions League form as Barcelona defeated Sabah 4-1 in Baku, while Gavi used the opportunity to underline his importance to Hansi Flick’s squad despite limited playing time this season. Adeyemi replaced the absent Lamine Yamal and delivered another influential performance, scoring after a superb assist from Alejandro Balde. The German forward has now scored in three of Barcelona’s five Champions League matches, strengthening his case as an important attacking option during the club’s demanding schedule. Adeyemi makes the most of Lamine Yamal’s absence Adeyemi’s goal was a positive contribution after Flick trusted him to cover for Yamal, and after the match, the forward said he was pleased to help Barcelona secure the three points. “The goal means a lot to me; I’m pleased for the team that I was able to help secure the win, and we can be happy with the three points,” he began. The German also recognised the challenge of playing away from home and praised Anthony Gordon, who scored twice against Sabah. “It’s always difficult to play away from home; they did a great job and were very motivated. Gordon? He had a very good game; I’m happy for the team and for him, and I hope he keeps scoring more goals.” Karim Adeyemi scored from Alejandro Balde’s assist. (Picture credit: X/@FCBarcelona) Adeyemi then insisted Barcelona have enough quality to cope without their teenage star. “He’s an important player and we have the quality to replace him. At Barça, there must always be replacements, regardless of the position. “We mustn’t rely on anyone or be afraid of anyone. We’re here to win and we want to win every match.” Gavi insists he remains important despite reduced minutes Gavi made his third start of the season against Sabah and played 86 minutes, offering Flick another opportunity to assess the midfielder’s readiness for a greater role. The Spain international acknowledged his importance within the squad while recognising that every player must understand their responsibilities. “Every player is important and everyone needs to be clear about their role. I consider myself important even though I’m not getting as many minutes at the moment, and I must always contribute to the team,” Gavi emphasised. The midfielder also reflected on the difficult experiences that have shaped his mentality, including serious injuries and his early days at La Masia. Gavi made his third Barcelona start of the season. (Picture credit: X/@FCBarcelona) “It might sound a bit boastful coming from me, but I think my mentality is unique. “Despite the serious injuries I’ve suffered and the difficult years I’ve had in the past – such as when I was on my own at La Masia, which wasn’t easy either – I’ve always pulled through on my own, by my own efforts.” Gavi embraces competition at Barcelona Gavi made clear that competition for places is part of representing Barcelon

item.title: Scott Gardner proud of the performance despite Fleetwood defeat
item.description: Scott Gardner proud of the performance despite Fleetwood defeat Leeds United Under-21s saw their Jersey Mike's Trophy campaign end in the group stages, after a defeat away at Fleetwood Town on Wednesday evening. The Sky Bet League Two side secured the three points they needed to progress into the knock-out stages, in a game that was all to play for. Scott Gardner's young side had put themselves in with a chance of qualification, but needed a result on the night at the Highbury Stadium, which ultimately they did not get. Speaking after the game, Gardner reflected on a spirited performance from his team. He said: "I thought we were very good and I thought we deserved something from the game. “We looked much more like ourselves tonight compared to the Oldham game and we had enough moments to win it. “But, you know, those moments are key, so if you don't take your chances, senior players find a way. They got two goals in the last 10 minutes, it's a shame for the players, but there’s loads we can take from it. “We knew that there was a respect from them [Fleetwood] and obviously a desire to go through. But our players showed they're more than capable across the board, and hopefully people can see that and the effort they put in. “I'm really proud of this group and how they work every day and wanted to get through, but we have to go again. I am disappointed for them they haven't got the reward of going through, but, you know, credit for how they performed.”

item.title: Knee surgery rules Sinner out of Australian Open
item.description: Jannik Sinner is a five-time Grand Slam champion [Getty Images] Jannik Sinner has been ruled out of the Australian Open in January following an operation on his knee. The 25-year-old Italian, who won the 2024 and 2025 titles at Melbourne Park, has not played competitively since winning Wimbledon on 12 July. In a social media post on Tuesday, world number two Sinner said he had undergone surgery to "improve the condition of my iliotibial band" - a thick band of tissue that runs along the outside of the knee. "We've been in regular touch with Jannik's team and they've confirmed he won't be joining us for the AO [Australian Open] in January following his recent surgery," said Tennis Australia chief executive Andrew Abdo. "Jannik loves competing here in Melbourne and is looking forward to returning for AO 2028. We wish him all the very best with his recovery and look forward to seeing him back on court soon." The 2027 Australian Open main draw starts on 17 January. Sinner's challenge at the 2026 tournament was ended by a five-set semi-final defeat by Novak Djokovic. Sinner was the dominant player for the first half of the season, winning 44 and losing just three of his singles matches. He won five Masters 1000 titles in a row between March and May, becoming the youngest man to complete the 'career Golden Masters', and reclaimed the world's top ranking from Alcaraz along the way. However, he suffered a shock second-round exit at the French Open, with Zverev ultimately stepping up to win his first Grand Slam title. Sinner bounced back on the grass courts, demolishing Novak Djokovic in the semi-finals before coming back from a set down against Zverev in the Wimbledon showpiece. He ended his season in early October, meaning he was unable to defend the points he claimed with title triumphs in China, Vienna, Paris and the ATP Finals at the end of 2025. Zverev went on to win the US Open and secure the year-end number one ranking. item.title: 'Unacceptable': Major economies push back against new US tariffs
item.description: China, the European Union and other major trading partners on Thursday criticised new US tariffs of up to 20 percent proposed by US President Donald Trump after a probe into alleged global overcapacity, raising the prospect of fresh trade tensions with allies and rivals alike.

item.title: CIAC football playoff update: Nine spots remain entering Thanksgiving Day's games
item.description: Burning the midnight oil on CIAC football playoff points in the office of GametimeCT editor Sean Patrick Bowley (Sean Patrick Bowley/Hearst Connecticut Media) Five more teams unofficially clinched CIAC playoff spots Wednesday night, according to GametimeCT projections, bringing the state-wide total to 39 and leaving nine berths remaining heading into Thanksgiving Day's games. Our projections are determined using the CIAC playoff formula , using OpenAI's GPT-6 Luna medium model and verified by GametimeCT using the current CIAC football playoff standings . Twenty eight games are scheduled for Thanksgiving morning. Here's a quick breakdown of who clinched and who needs what to join the field of 48 Thursday morning. CIAC PLAYOFF RANKINGS: CLASS LL | CLASS L | CLASS MM | CLASS M | CLASS SS | CLASS S The points are not official until the CIAC football playoff committee meets and approves the final tally the day after all the games are completed on Thanksgiving Day. The Playoff Picture CLASS LL (6 of 8 clinched) SOUTH WINDSOR's 42-21 victory over Enfield kept it alive for a Class LL playoff spot. The Bobcats' hopes now hinge on the Green Bowl and NFA (5-4)-New London If HAMDEN (5-4) beats Notre Dame, the Green Dragons will clinch. NFA needs any of Griswold/Wheeler, Woodstock, East Lyme or Fitch to win and clinch over South Windsor. SOUTHINGTON (8-1) clinches the No. 1 seed with a win over Cheshire, STAPLES (7-2) and GREENWICH (6-3) play with the winner looking at the No. 2 seed unless Southington loses or NEW BRITAIN (8-2) gets enough bonus help to pass them. DANBURY (5-4) is likely into the No. 5 seed and FAIRFIELD PREP (6-4) will likely be the No.6, unless NFA beats New London to clinch and enough bonuses to catch either. CLASS L (6 of 8 clnched) NEW CANAAN (7-2) clinched due to Xavier's loss to Fairfield Prep on Tuesday night, leaving two spots remaining. Farmington's late, 33-28 loss to Plainville and Warde and Ridgefield's losses eliminated those teams from playoff contention, leaving four teams. DARIEN (6-3) is win/in vs. New Canaan in the Turkey Bowl. Failing that, they'll fall into a four-team race for the final two spots and be in trouble, unless both Maloney and Notre Dame lose. MALONEY (6-3), vs. Platt in the Stoddard bowl) and NOTRE DAME-WEST HAVEN (6-3, vs. Hamden in the Green Bowl) will both clinch the final two spots if Darien loses. If Darien wins, it'll be a bonus race between them, with Maloney holding the edge. Notre Dame must get all of its bonus games, so Notre Dame would prefer a Darien loss to get in with a win. CHENEY TECH (7-3) needs both Platt and Notre Dame to lose. CLASS MM (6 of 8 clinched) MIDDLETOWN (7-3) clinched a playoff spot after Tuesday night's results, leaving two spots remaining. TORRINGTON (6-3) will clinch with a victory over Watertown and PLATT (6-3) will clinch with a victory over Maloney. XAVIER (6-4) needs one of them to lose and to get enough bonus help to stay ahead of WILTON (6-4) to claim the final spot.

item.title: Lions’ late owner Martha Firestone Ford will be on Matthew Stafford’s mind as he watches ex-team play on Thanksgiving
item.description: Los Angeles Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford talks with former Detroit Lions owner Martha Firestone Ford. For years, Thanksgiving in the Stafford household meant watching Dad play quarterback for the Detroit Lions. Even after Matthew Stafford joined the Rams, his wife and daughters still had to share him with football. At some point every Turkey Day, he was due at practice. That was Thanksgiving for Stafford. He was either playing in a game or preparing for one. Matthew Stafford throws a pass during the Rams’ 26-13 win over the Packers on Nov. 25, 2026, at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, Calif. Getty Images This year, the Rams got their work done Wednesday night against the Packers in the NFL’s inaugural Thanksgiving Eve game. For the first time in as long as he can remember, Stafford gets the whole day with his family. And when the Lions come on, his wife and daughters can slide over and make room for Dad on the couch. “I’ll be tuning in just like everybody else,” Stafford said. Except there’s someone he’ll be thinking about when his old team takes the field. Martha Firestone Ford, the Lions’ owner and chair emeritus, died this week . And for all the pleasure Stafford takes in the prospect of a Thanksgiving at home, he said he’ll be “a little heavy-hearted” watching the Lions play. He was a kid from Texas by way of the University of Georgia when the Lions made him the first pick in the 2009 NFL draft. Ford had been part of the organization since 1963, when she and her husband, William Clay Ford, purchased the team. By the time Stafford came along, she had spent nearly half a century welcoming people to Detroit. Detroit owner Martha Firestone Ford, who died this week, plays with Sawyer Stafford, held by her mother Kelly Stafford, before a home game against the Falcons. USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect He remembers how warmly she welcomed him and his family. “She’s a special lady to me, to my family, and to that organization to the city of Detroit,” Stafford said. He spent his first 12 NFL seasons there. Along the way, he got to see another side of the woman who had made him feel at home. When her husband died in 2014, Ford took over the Lions herself. The relationship Stafford built with Ford has made her passing all the more painful. Even as he prepared to play the Packers, his heart was with his second family in Detroit. “I’ve reached out to them a little bit,” Stafford said. “Just an unbelievable lady, a great leader, and she’ll be missed.” Even after the trade to Los Angeles, Thursdays in November generally meant practice for the next opponent. It took the NFL putting the Rams and Packers in its inaugural Thanksgiving Eve game Wednesday to give Stafford the first full Thanksgiving off he can remember in years. Matthew Stafford waves to the crowd after the Rams’ 26-13 win over the Packers on Nov. 25, 2026, at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, Calif. item.title: Spurs Fall To Trail Blazers In NBA Cup Despite Wemby’s Monster Game: 4 Things We Learned
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Jaime Valdez-Imagn Images Victor Wembanyama did everything he could to carry the San Antonio Spurs to an NBA Cup victory, but it wasn’t enough to overcome the Portland Trail Blazers . Despite a monster 44-point, 16-rebound performance from their superstar, the Spurs fell 116-111 in a game decided by Portland’s efficiency on both ends. Wembanyama was spectacular, shooting 17-30 from the field and adding two blocks while playing 35 minutes. Devin Vassell added 18 points, and Stephon Castle finished with 20 points and nine assists. But San Antonio struggled to find consistency from beyond the arc, connecting on just 10-36 three-point attempts. Just an ugly shooting night. Portland had their own stars show up. Deni Avdija erupted for 33 points, 12 rebounds, and seven assists, while Damian Lillard added 29 points and seven assists. The Trail Blazers also received 16 points from Sidy Cissoko and 11 from Jrue Holiday off the bench. Here are four things we learned from San Antonio’s disappointing NBA Cup loss. 1. Victor Wembanyama Is Nearly Impossible To Stop Wembanyama had an extraordinary performance, and the numbers barely do justice to how much San Antonio relied on him. The Spurs superstar finished with 44 points and 16 rebounds on 17-30 shooting. He also knocked down three three-pointers, converted seven free throws, and recorded two blocks. Portland had no reliable answer for him individually. Wembanyama found easy ways to score and looked like the best player in the world tonight. He also finished with a +2 rating despite San Antonio losing by five points. That is particularly telling when considering how much the Spurs struggled to generate offense outside their primary contributors. The frustrating part for San Antonio is that a 44-point, 16-rebound performance from Wembanyama should normally put a team in an excellent position to win. Instead, the Spurs wasted one of his best performances by failing to provide enough shooting around him. 2. Deni Avdija And Damian Lillard Were A Dynamic Offensive Duo Portland’s victory was built around two outstanding performances from Avdija and Lillard. Avdija was arguably the most complete player on the floor outside Wembanyama, finishing with 33 points, 12 rebounds, and seven assists. He shot 11-21 from the field and 5-8 from three-point range, giving the Spurs problems from virtually every area of the court. Lillard provided another major scoring threat, recording 29 points and seven assists. Although he shot just 7-20 overall, he made five three-pointers and converted all 10 of his free-throw attempts. Together, they combined for 62 points and 14 assists. That production gave Portland enough offensive firepower to withstand Wembanyama’s monster night. The difference was that the Trail Blazers had two players consistently creating opportunities, while San Antonio leaned heavily on its superstar. 3. item.title: 10 Takeaways: Devon Toews Continues to Quietly Put Together a Special Season (+)
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect There have been plenty of positives to take away from how the Colorado Avalanche have played lately. Ever since Nathan MacKinnon was injured , which came moments after Cale Makar ‘s injury, the Avs have seemingly tightened up their game. Maybe they were overly reliant on their superstars and needed to get a little uncomfortable. Or maybe it’s what Jared Bednar talked about weeks ago, that veteran teams sometimes need a little time to get going. Either way, something is working. The Avalanche got Makar back against the Montreal Canadiens on Wednesday and went on to complete a 6-0 rout of one of the best teams in the Eastern Conference. Makar wasn’t the biggest difference-maker in this one. It wasn’t even Mackenzie Blackwood , who helped the Avs record their third consecutive shutout win on home ice by making 27 saves. It was Devon Toews . The Avalanche’s veteran defenseman has been magnificent this season and continued that trend against the Canadiens. Toews scored two of Colorado’s six goals. He also played 22:59, including 4:50 on the power play. One of his goals came on the man advantage where he’s currently quarterbacking the top unit. Read Next Landeskog Calls Out Canadiens’ Late-Game Antics After Avalanche Blowout 1. I find it strange that several people around the hockey world have, in some ways, written off the Avalanche after some of the bad games they had in October. It’s been a while since we’ve seen a brutal loss in Columbus or Nashville, or a terrible game in Philadelphia. But it feels like many have already made up their minds about what this team is. Which, in a sense, is fine. I was among the people last year who thought the Vegas Golden Knights weren’t a threat. But then they hired John Tortorella, went on a run to get into the playoffs, and led the Stanley Cup Final 2-1 before losing three straight. They obviously swept the Avs to get there. The Avalanche, at least for now, aren’t having nearly as bad a season as the Knights were early last year, so it’s not an apples-to-apples comparison. It’s just interesting to see how many people still aren’t talking about them, even after they’ve righted the ship with their defensive play, goaltending, and overall team game. 2. Goaltending has bounced back in the best possible way. Mackenzie Blackwood has been incredible for the better part of the last six weeks, and this was his second shutout of the season. Not only did it come right after Scott Wedgewood recorded his first of the year, but it also followed a 4-1 loss in Utah that Blackwood needed to bounce back from. The Avalanche’s starting goalie improved to 12-4-1 with a .910 save percentage. He made some nice saves early in the third period to keep the shutout intact. 3. What a run at Ball Arena lately. The Avs have three straight shutouts at home, starting with a 4-0 victory over the Detroit Red Wings on Nov. 4. item.title: Maxx Crosby sends clear message on Deshaun Watson ahead of Browns showdown
item.description: Credit: Mitchell Leff/Jared C. Tilton via Getty Images Maxx Crosby has made his feelings clear on Deshaun Watson ahead of the Las Vegas Raiders’ clash with the Cleveland Browns, describing the quarterback as a major threat. The Raiders are preparing for their first primetime appearance of the season, with their defence facing the challenge of containing Watson and his ability to make plays both through the air and on the ground. Watson impressed in his previous outing against the Houston Texans, completing 25 of 40 passes for 312 yards while adding 49 rushing yards and a touchdown on eight carries. Maxx Crosby explains why Deshaun Watson poses a major threat Crosby knows the Raiders will need to be at their best to limit the Browns quarterback, who has shown he can create problems even when a play breaks down. Speaking to reporters , the Las Vegas defensive star praised Watson’s physical attributes and ability to lead Cleveland’s offence. “[Watson is] a dual-threat guy,” Crosby said. “He’s had a lot of success in this league. He’s got a really strong arm, tough, mobile, and can make a lot of off-schedule plays. He can obviously process as well. “He’s a really good quarterback [and] is leading those guys, and I’ve got a lot of respect for his game. We know it’s another challenge. He’s a really good guy, and for us, we’ve got to be at our best to slow him down and mess up his day.” Crosby also admitted the Raiders are excited about playing under the primetime spotlight, although he knows the pressure is on his team to deliver. “We’re fired up,” he added. “It’s awesome. You want to play on the biggest stages against the best team.” The defensive end described the situation as “do or die” for Las Vegas, with the team desperate to secure a significant win before its bye week. Meanwhile, former Browns player Hanford Dixon believes Cleveland should win the matchup but admitted he has concerns about Raiders quarterback Fernando Mendoza. Dixon suggested the rookie has started to look more comfortable in the pocket and is beginning to understand the demands of the position. That gives Cleveland another challenge to consider, even with Crosby making it clear that stopping Watson will be a major priority for the Raiders. item.title: Trail Blazers Player Ratings: Damian Lillard And Deni Avdija Combine For 62 Points To Topple Spurs
item.description: Nov 25, 2026; Portland, Oregon, USA; Portland Trail Blazers forward Deni Avdija (8) reacts after scoring against the San Antonio Spurs during the second half at Moda Center. Mandatory Credit: Jaime Valdez-Imagn Images The Portland Trail Blazers (12-6) have earned the reputation of a dark horse in the West this season. While this may be true, their 116-111 victory against the San Antonio Spurs in Wednesday night’s NBA Cup matchup should see them rated as a genuine threat in the West. The Trail Blazers looked dominant against the Spurs. Although the game was neck-and-neck for the most part, Portland’s tenacity and unwillingness to give up eventually broke down San Antonio’s defense, as they outscored the Spurs 32-24 in the fourth quarter to secure the win. Portland’s winning effort was led by the pair of Deni Avdija and Damian Lillard , who combined for a whopping 62 points. Aside from them, the late-game contributions of Jrue Holiday and the scoring boost by Scoot Henderson played a vital role in sealing the deal. The Spurs also had some standout performers, with Victor Wembanyama (44 PTS, 16 REB, 2 BLK) and Stephon Castle (20 PTS, 6 REB, 9 AST) outscoring the Blazers’ duo with a combined 64 points. Unfortunately, with solid contributions across the board, Portland would not be denied this win. In light of this, we examine and rate the performance of each Blazers player that participated in the win. Deni Avdija: A+ Game Stats: 33 PTS, 12 REB, 7 AST, 2 STL, 2 TOV, 11-21 FG, 5-8 3-PT FG, 6-8 FT, 36 MIN There is virtually no questioning how vital Deni Avdija was for the Blazers on Wednesday night. Along with his monster 33-point performance to pave the way for Portland, Avdija played some solid defense and placed an incredible amount of pressure on San Antonio’s wings. His efficiency from beyond the arc effectively opened up the game for the Blazers. Given that he also banked in a clutch three-pointer to give Portland a sizable lead, the forward was the driving force behind the team’s success. Damian Lillard: A+ Game Stats: 29 PTS, 3 REB, 6 AST, 2 STL, 2 TOV, 7-20 FG, 5-12 3-PT FG, 10-10 FT, 34 MIN Like Avdija, Damian Lillard played an equally important role in securing success for the Portland Trail Blazers. Lillard’s three-point shooting and playmaking were among the factors that helped Portland remain within striking distance in the first half. Although Lillard played a relatively more passive role in the second half, the veteran guard remained a factor on offense. With a crucial three-pointer to extend Portland’s lead to four points (93-89) early in the fourth quarter, Lillard laid the foundations for the Trail Blazers’ consistent production in the final frame. Sidy Cissoko: A Game Stats: 16 PTS, 4 REB, 2 AST, 2 STL, 1 BLK, 6-14 FG, 4-10 3-PT FG, 30 MIN Since earning a consistent role as a starter for the Trail Blazers, Sidy Cissoko has been somewhat inconsistent offensively. item.title: ‘Craziest Day in Sports,’ ‘NBA Gotta Mic This Up’ — Hoops Fans Erupt As Dillon Brooks Gets Tossed Out After Heated Face-to-Face Spat With Kevin Durant
item.description: Fans react after Dillon Brooks is ejected following a heated exchange with Kevin Durant during the Rockets' win over the Suns. Phoenix Suns forward Dillon Brooks was ejected from Wednesday’s 116-104 loss to the Houston Rockets after getting into a heated exchange with Kevin Durant in the closing seconds. The confrontation quickly drew reactions online, with fans weighing in on another tense moment between the two. Brooks already had a technical foul when he and the 16-time All-Star squared up with 23.8 seconds remaining. The second technical sent Brooks to the locker room. Durant stayed in the game and scored Houston’s final points on a dunk off an Amen Thompson assist with three seconds left. Fans React to Dillon Brooks and Kevin Durant’s Latest Heated Exchange BrickCenter posted video of the confrontation , writing that the two “stopped playing MID GAME to trash talk each other.” BGN Hoops had a reaction of its own: “This is what the league is missing. Bring back real rivalries.” One fan replied to BrickCenter’s clip, “If you don’t like that, you don’t like NBA basketballlll.” Another response read , “Looks like this came out of NBA 2K. Love this. Durant has grown on me, but still took the easy way out, unfortunately.” The tension between Brooks and Durant goes back to their days as opponents in the Western Conference. Brooks was still with the Memphis Grizzlies when the two began exchanging words on the court. Their March 30, 2025, meeting between the Rockets and Suns ended with officials throwing Brooks out after an altercation with the two-time NBA Finals MVP. The two eventually switched teams in a seven-team trade in July 2025. Houston acquired Durant, while Phoenix received Brooks, Jalen Green, and other assets. Their differences also surfaced online last month. Durant and Suns governor Mat Ishbia exchanged posts after Ishbia revisited Phoenix’s decision to acquire KD in 2023. Durant then made an apparent reference to Brooks’ DUI arrest, prompting the Suns forward to enter the exchange with an Instagram post of his own. Brooks posted an Instagram story thanking Ishbia for “cleaning up that stench in the locker room before I came.” He did not mention Durant by name, but the post was widely interpreted as a shot at the two-time NBA champion. SEE ALSO: ‘Mid Without the Bluetooth Fouls,’ ‘His Signature Move, the Flop’ – NBA Fans Troll Shai Gilgeous-Alexander After Failed Foul-Baiting Attempt vs. Timberwolves The teams had already met earlier in November, with Phoenix taking a 102-99 win on Nov. 7. Durant finished that game 5-for-14 from the field, while Brooks scored 11 points for the Suns. Another fan wrote , “NBA gotta mic … this up.” One viewer asked , “Craziest day in sports since when?” A final reaction read , “Me and my ex seeing each other at a bar.” Brooks finished Wednesday’s game with 12 points, 6 rebounds and 4 assists in 31 minutes. item.title: Blazers hand Spurs first road loss after Deni Avdija’s dagger
item.description: Credit: Jaime Valdez-Imagn Images Blazers hand Spurs first road loss after Deni Avdija’s dagger appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Portland Trail Blazers must have encircled the 25th of November on their calendar seeing as this would be their first time this season that they’ll be facing off against the San Antonio Spurs , the team that eliminated them from the 2026 NBA playoffs. And in the end, the Blazers got some sweet revenge as they defeated the Spurs in NBA Cup group stage action, 116-111, thanks to a dagger triple from Deni Avdija. The game was still hanging in the balance with around 40 seconds remaining in the fourth quarter. The Blazers were leading by just two points, 111-109, and the Spurs put the clamps on them for the first 20 seconds of the shot clock. But Avdija’s prayer was answered. Letting a three-pointer fly with the shot clock winding down, Avdija banked in a triple to push Portland’s lead to five, and the Spurs would not recover from that finishing blow — suffering their first road loss of the season in the process. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) WHAT??? Deni Avdija BANKS IN A THREE-POINT LEAD TO GIVE THE BLAZERS A 5-POINT LEAD 🎯 pic.twitter.com/3zLQu8xlVm — ClutchPoints (@ClutchPoints) November 26, 2026 The Spurs still had an opportunity to retaliate after that triple from Avdija, but Julian Champagnie missed a three-pointer off a timeout. Even though Toumani Camara turned the ball over on the subsequent possession and Champagnie made a layup to cut Portland’s lead to just three, the Blazers played it smart for their final possession. They held on to the ball, and Camara made amends for his turnover by making two free throws to ice the game. With their NBA Cup win over the Spurs, the Blazers now stand tall in Group C. Even though the Spurs still have the best point differential among the four teams that are currently 2-1 in group stage action, the Blazers own the tiebreaker against them thanks to this huge victory. The Blazers will be closing out the group stage against the Golden State Warriors, while the Spurs will be facing the Los Angeles Lakers in the potential game to decide which team makes it to the next round of the competition. item.title: Everton Have Centre-Back Decision To Make: It's Simple
item.description: Everton head into their game against Liverpool in the Merseyside derby without their captain James Tarkowski. The English centre-back was sent off against Brentford in the Premier League on Monday night, meaning he will be suspended for the game on Sunday. It's a huge blow for Everton to lose not only one of their starting centre-backs but also their captain in such a big fixture. That's why many are incredibly disappointed in Tarkowski , not only for contributing to us losing against Brentford, but also due to the suspension that comes with it. Thankfully for the Toffees, Jarrad Branthwaite appeared to come through the game without any injuries. Otherwise, it would be a disastrous situation at the back for Everton . David Moyes does have a decision to make at the back, though, as it's not a foregone conclusion who's going to replace Tarkowski. We go over the potential options that Moyes has and which would be the best for the derby. Jake O'Brien Spot On As He Discusses Everton Defeat vs Brentford There was little excuse for Everton's heavy 4-0 defeat against Brentford on Monday night, and Jake O'Brien is refusing to hide behind the red card for James Tarkowski. Everton's centre-back problem Moyes does have multiple options to replace Tarkowski at centre-back against Liverpool on Sunday. When Tarkowski was sent off against Brentford, Jake O'Brien slotted in at centre-back. Merlin Rohl moved to right-back, a position he's played multiple times so far this season. Bringing O'Brien in to replace Tarkowski is one option, and then you can either play Rohl or Ainsley Maitland-Niles at right-back. James Garner is also a potential option at right-back, especially given he's not always been at the races this season in central midfield. Another option for Moyes will be to bring in Michael Keane, and then that allows him to keep O'Brien at right-back. Keane has a lack of minutes for Everton this season, so throwing him in in a Merseyside derby would be a bold decision from Moyes. O'Brien is clearly Moyes' preferred right-back, though, so bringing in Keane would allow him to continue playing him there. In reality, the only two options are Keane and O'Brien for the centre-back position, and depending on which one is selected, that impacts who comes in at right-back. Maitland-Niles has also had a lack of minutes, so throwing him in in a Merseyside derby also might not be a smart move. The best solution To find the best solution, you first of all have to consider which player to play at centre-back. In reality, it should be O'Brien, especially with Keane's lack of minutes this season. Keane is prone to making errors, and it wouldn't be fair on him to thrust him into a Merseyside derby. Although O'Brien has predominantly played right-back, at least he's getting regular minutes at the moment. This then moves us on to who replaces O'Brien at right-back for Everton . It wouldn't be a surprise

item.title: Gabriel Jesus happy with his goal but not his performance for Barcelona against Sabah
item.description: Barcelona's Brazilian forward #09 Gabriel Jesus reacts during the UEFA Champions League match between Sabah and Barcelona at the Baku Olympic Stadium in Baku on November 25, 2026. (Photo by Igor IVANKO / AFP via Getty Images) | AFP via Getty Images Gabriel Jesus was happy with his goal but not his performance in Barcelona’s 4-1 win over Sabah in the Champions League on Wednesday. The summer signing was in the starting XI for the match as Hansi Flick rotated his side and did get on his scoresheet. Speaking afterwards, Jesus explained why he had found it tough going in Baku against Sabah. “It’s always difficult, the Champions League is. Obviously, everyone can talk about Barça, but if Sabah is in the competition, it’s because they have a good team. We have played some players who haven’t participated as much in recent matches. We have won, I’m happy about the goal but not so much about my performance. Happy, but I hope I can keep helping the team,” he told reporters. “Normally, when players who haven’t been playing as much, it’s hard to find the rhythm, and at the start of the match I think it showed. This is part of the game.” Jesus admitted he’s well aware that he’s a squad player but he’s still hoping for more minutes as the season progresses. “We are here to help Barça become a better team. I understand my situation and try to stay in shape. Training without playing is complicated, but that’s how it is. We try to help, the decision is Flick’s. Scoring goals is always good,” he added. “The goal is very important. I always want to score goals. My role is different. Rapha is scoring a lot and is very important to us. I want to keep having opportunities, minutes. Even if I don’t play well, it’s important to be there to score.” Barcelona now head back to Spain to prepare for Sunday’s La Liga match against Deportivo.

item.title: Navajo Stirling & Carlos Ulberg Make Decision on Future UFC Fight
item.description: Navajo Stirling Carlos Ulberg UFC Getty UFC light heavyweight teammates Navajo Stirling and Carlos Ulberg have made a decision about a future fight against each other. Ulberg is the current UFC light heavyweight champion, while Stirling is one of the top contenders in the weight class following his KO win over Jiri Prochazka at UFC Qatar — the same man whom Ulberg beat to collect the title back in April at UFC 327. These two men should fight for the belt next. But with both fighters training at City Kickboxing in Auckland, New Zealand, it makes things a bit more difficult. Now, we know what their decision is. Navajo Stirling Won’t Fight Carlos Ulberg According to CKB head coach Eugene Bareman , the team has decided that Stirling will not fight Ulberg, even if the belt is on the line. “Boys from the same gym don’t fight. We’ve had this agreement from the very beginning of the gym. Some things are bigger than fighting. Friendship and the bond you’ve built with someone are bigger than fighting,” Bareman said. 🚨🏆Eugene Bareman confirms Carlos Ulberg and Navajo Stirling will NOT fight each other for the title: “Boys from the same gym don't fight. We've had this agreement from the very beginning of the gym. Some things are bigger than fighting. Friendship and the bond you've built… pic.twitter.com/Hrzfbr8lwi — Home of Fight (@Home_of_Fight) November 26, 2026 Team Holding Navajo Stirling Back Based on this decision, it seems like Stirling is being held back from doing what he set out to do when he first became an MMA fighter, which is to win the UFC title. There is no doubt that this is a difficult situation for the team and for both fighters involved, because MMA is partly a team sport. But it’s also an individual sport, and the team choosing for these two not to fight each other is holding Stirling back from testing himself against the champ. For Ulberg, this is an easier decision, because as the champion he has other contenders whom he can fight, such as Magomed Ankalaev. But for Stirling, the decision not to fight his teammate is one that could change the trajectory of his entire career. It will be interesting to hear what UFC president Dana White has to say about this, because he’s always said in the past that MMA fighters need to look out for themselves, and in this case, it looks like the team is putting Ulberg first. This article was originally published on HEAVY The post Navajo Stirling & Carlos Ulberg Make Decision on Future UFC Fight appeared first on HEAVY .

item.title: Packers QB Jordan Love shares honest self-assessment of multi-INT game vs. Rams
item.description: Lon Horwedel-Imagn Images Packers QB Jordan Love shares honest self-assessment of multi-INT game vs. Rams appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Blake Corum and the Los Angeles Rams completely overwhelmed the Green Bay Packers on Wednesday, handing them their second consecutive loss. The Packers, including star quarterback Jordan Love , failed to live up to expectations against an injury-hit Rams team. Love himself was also disappointed with his performance and didn’t shy away from acknowledging his mistakes. During the postgame press conference, Love took responsibility for both of his interceptions. He explained that Matthew Golden had been rerouted on one of the plays, while he had already thrown the ball toward the intended spot, resulting in the costly mistake. The Packers quarterback finished the game completing 17 of 29 pass attempts for 198 yards, one touchdown, and two interceptions. The game marked his first with multiple interceptions this season. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Love admitted that his overall showing fell short of what the team needed to come away with a victory. “Not good enough,” Love said. The Packers star quarterback also said that he needed to lead by example and perform better. “We dropped the ball, especially on offense. It starts with me. I gotta be better,” he added. The Packers also faced a major injury setback as wide receiver Christian Watson left the game with a concussion . Watson had made a significant impact in the first half, recording four receptions for 65 yards. However, Green Bay’s offense struggled to maintain its momentum after Watson’s departure. The Packers were held scoreless in the second half while the Rams put up 13 unanswered points and piled up 241 rushing yards. Green Bay will now aim to turn things around when it travels to take on the New Orleans Saints in Week 13. Following back-to-back losses, the Packers need to deliver a much-improved offensive performance and take better care of the football if they want to keep their postseason hopes on track. item.title: Why Wu-Tang Clan is performing during halftime at Bears vs. Lions NFL Thanksgiving game
item.description: Why Wu-Tang Clan is performing during halftime at Bears vs. Lions NFL Thanksgiving game originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Of all the performers the NFL has enlisted to rock the stage on Thanksgiving Day, few have paired style with substance quite like Wu-Tang Clan. The Staten Island-based outfit appears to be the largest act the NFL has booked in terms of number of members, with nine contributors — RZA, GZA, Inspectah Deck, U-God, Ghostface Killah, Method Man, Raekwon, Masta Killa and Cappadonna — expected to feature in some way during Bears vs. Lions . So, just why did Wu-Tang Clan get the call over other noteworthy acts, some of whom call Motown home? Here's a look at why the NFL opted to give the rap group the nod in the first game of the Thanksgiving Day slate. MORE: Meet the full list of 2026 NFL Thanksgiving performers, from U2 to national anthem singers Why Wu-Tang Clan is performing during halftime at Bears vs. Lions NFL Thanksgiving game Wu-Tang Clan is one of rap's seminal acts, a dizzying blend of lyricism and gritty deliveries that helped put East Coast rap on the map in the early-1990s. The group hasn't released in album in more than a decade. Still, the brand remains as relevant as ever, influencing legions of rappers young and old. Wu-Tang Clan charmed listeners with its first release, "Enter the Wu-Tang: 36 Chambers" in 1993, a titan of a project headlined by "C.R.E.A. M." and "Protect Ya Neck." An underground release that centered around our protagonists' experiences growing up in New York, "Enter the Wu-Tang" didn't project to garner much airplay. The content — namely its humor and imagery — proved too difficult for listeners to ignore. By 1995, the album was certified Platinum and 30 years on, it has sold more than four million records. Those sales were no aberration. The project is adorned with kung-fu references, musings on the Nation of Islam and good old-fashion braggadocio. MORE: Best NFL Thanksgiving halftime shows ever, ranked from Creed to Dolly Parton "This is the sound of accidental fame," wrote Pitchfork's Rollie Pemberton in a retrospective review. "Something as unique and unusual as this record isn't supposed to find itself at the height of commercial viability; it's supposed to smolder underground, hidden from the view of mainstream America, who surely would not be ready for such a challenge. But America was ready, in part because this one challenged convention, not listeners." The album — and its follow-up, "Wu-Tang Forever" — remains tethered to the public consciousness, as does the myriad solo projects crafted by the group's nine members. Predictably, the group is getting its due, best encapsulated by its recent induction into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame. Wu-Tang Clan isn't your typical Thanksgiving Day performers. But its pronounced impact on rap, music and pop culture more broadly can't be denied. That seems to have been enough to land

item.title: Entire Real Madrid squad working to help Brazilian regain his confidence – report
item.description: Entire Real Madrid squad working to help Brazilian regain his confidence – report This hasn’t been a great season for Vinicius Jr., who appears to have fallen behind in the pecking order for the first time during his spell at Real Madrid. The forward missed four important La Liga matches due to suspension while his performances in other competitions haven’t exactly been top-notch. Vinicius Jr. himself is aware of his situation at Real Madrid and is working hard to get back to full potential. Entire Real Madrid team at work The international break has helped Vinicius Jr. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) According to MARCA (h/t Madrid Xtra ), the entire Real Madrid team is currently involved in helping Vinicius Jr. regain his confidence after a poor start to the season. This was made evident when Kylian Mbappe gifted his Man of the Match trophy, in the win over PSV Eindhoven, to the Brazilian international. Vinicius Jr. has so far scored two goals and three assists in 14 matches across all competitions, which is not the kind of output Real Madrid were expecting when the renewed the player’s contract in the summer. Nevertheless, it appears Vinicius Jr. has the backing of the coach Jose Mourinho as well as the rest of his teammates. A slow but steady progress All eyes on Vinicius Jr.’s progress. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) To Real Madrid’s fortune, it appears Vinicius Jr. has started making steady progress, especially after the second international break of the season. The explosive forward produced some excellent performances for the Brazilian national team under Carlo Ancelotti. The game-time he got under Ancelotti during the break was extremely useful. Vinicius Jr. returned with yet another impressive performance cameo against Celta Vigo. Although he wasn’t involved in goal, he did start in the game against PSV. The forward ultimately scored his first goal for Real Madrid in three months in the 5-1 win over PSV, prompting his teammate Mbappe to gift him the MOTM award. This is a positive sign for Los Blancos , who would ideally like to have Vinicius Jr. firing on all cylinders heading into a packed December schedule, where rotation could become essential. Jose Mourinho has already made Vinicius Jr.’s return as his utmost priority so it will be interesting to see whether or not the attacker gets more game-time in the coming weeks.

item.title: Women's World Cup 2027 MVPs: USWNT standout Trinity Rodman is ready to show the world what the fuss is all about
item.description: Trinity Rodman WWC MVPs GFX - Getty/GOAL The 24-year-old has starred in the NWSL and at the Olympic Games, winning both titles, and will be expected to spearhead the U.S. attack in Brazil this summer There are not many bigger stars in the world of women’s football than Trinity Rodman. Nothing highlights that quite like what unfolded at the turn of the year when clubs in Europe were circling as her contract with the Washington Spirit expired. Desperate not to lose one of the most talented and recognisable players in the league, the NWSL introduced its High Impact Player rule, quickly nicknamed ‘the Rodman rule’, in order to allow the Spirit to offer Rodman the sort of contract that could keep her around, making her the highest-paid women’s footballer in the world . How Rodman performed in the season that unfolded afterwards only served to justify the deal. A return of 14 goals and 10 assists helped fire the Spirit into the 2026 NWSL Championship game, in which she also scored despite her side’s eventual defeat . Though still only 25 years old, it’s not the first time Rodman has performed to an incredible level when all eyes were on her. Be it the way she marked herself out as a star in her own right during her rookie year, firing the Spirit to its first NWSL Championship crown after entering the league to much fanfare given her father Dennis’ status as a basketball icon, or her displays in the United States’ Olympic triumph in 2024 , which saw the national team respond remarkably well to the disappointments of the previous year’s World Cup, Rodman is no stranger to excelling under pressure. It all adds up to make her one of the most fascinating figures heading into the 2027 Women’s World Cup. Rodman has yet to really mark herself out on that stage, which is undoubtedly the biggest in the sport. But looking at her career to date, there are not many reasons to bet against her doing so in Brazil. Attention aplenty The spotlight was on Rodman in her first NWSL season, but she performed under that pressure, helping the Washington Spirit to win its first NWSL Championship title Rodman probably knew that she was never going to enter the world of women’s football quietly. When she became the youngest player to be drafted in NWSL history back in 2021, as an 18-year-old, it was her mother who stood proudly beside her, but it was her father’s name that added to the attention she would receive. It wasn’t until several years later that Rodman would fully air the frustrations that came with that, which went well beyond the irritation many children of famous sporting parents endure of simply wanting to be a star in their own right. "He's not a dad. Maybe by blood, but nothing else," she said on the Call Her Daddy podcast in 2024, explaining her father’s limited presence in her childhood and how her mother struggled financially to raise her two children, with them even living in their car at one point. item.title: Flick talks Gordon, Adeyemi, Jesus, Balde, Pedri, Olmo after Sabah 1-4 Barcelona
item.description: Flick talks Gordon, Adeyemi, Jesus, Balde, Pedri, Olmo after Sabah 1-4 Barcelona Hansi Flick was pleased with Barcelona’s 4-1 victory over Sabah in the UEFA Champions League, but the manager admitted that his side’s performance left room for improvement. The German coach highlighted Barcelona’s stronger second half, praised the contributions of Anthony Gordon, Karim Adeyemi and Gabriel Jesus, and explained why Pedri was withdrawn at half-time. Barcelona secured three important points in Baku, with Gordon scoring twice before Adeyemi and Jesus added further goals, although Flick’s post-match assessment made clear that the result was more satisfying than the overall display. Flick identifies Barcelona’s improvement after half-time Barcelona struggled to convert their possession into clear opportunities during the opening period, allowing Sabah to remain competitive before Gordon opened the scoring. Flick acknowledged the Azerbaijani side’s confidence and explained how Barcelona eventually took control. “They came out with a lot of confidence. We had possession in the first half. It took us a while to score the opening goal, but we finally did. And from then on, we took advantage of the rest of our chances.” The manager was particularly encouraged by the attacking contributions of Gordon, Adeyemi and Jesus, whose goals helped Barcelona secure a comfortable away victory. Anthony Gordon scored two goals against Sabah. (Picture credit: X/@FCBarcelona) “This is very good news. Gordon has been very important in pressing; Karim, too, and Gabriel has a lot of quality. It’s not easy facing someone like Raphinha, but his level is a positive sign.” Gabriel Jesus earns Flick’s backing despite limited minutes As stated, Jesus scored Barcelona’s fourth goal after Gordon’s double and Adeyemi’s strike had put the visitors firmly in control. Flick acknowledged that the Brazilian faces a difficult battle for regular opportunities, with Raphinha occupying an important position in his plans. “It’s not easy for Gabriel Jesus either, being behind Raphinha, who is very important for us. But I love the quality he has, and he’s always a positive player. “When he came here, I spoke with him and told him I didn’t know how things would go, that he might play fewer minutes. “He told me it was no problem, that he would work for the team. And now we have seven games left until the end of the year, and anything he can do to help us is welcome,” added the manager. Pedri’s substitution was planned as Flick monitors Balde Flick also clarified that Pedri’s half-time withdrawal was part of a prearranged workload plan, not a reaction to a fitness concern. Dani Olmo was also scheduled to play a specific amount of time. Pedri was taken off at half-time. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) “Pedri’s substitution was planned. He was supposed to play 45 minutes. Olmo’s substitution was also planned. “We were able to manage the minutes of other players and the result was as expected.” Barcelo

item.title: Ollie Bassett: Packington to Toronto and life as a professional footballer in Canada
item.description: Ollie Bassett Brits Abroad 16:9 - GOAL In the latest instalment of GOAL’s ‘Brits Abroad’ series, a man that has played in both hemispheres talks futsal, life Down Under, growing tired of plane travel and what to do in Canada There was a time not all that long ago when British footballers plying their trade abroad were rarer than hen’s teeth. Individual reluctance to leave geographical comfort zones led to collective wings being clipped. This is, however, a brave new world, with cultural advancement meaning that no corner of the planet should be considered too far-flung. Flying the nest and enjoying a different way of life is now an experience to be embraced, rather than feared. Of course there are challenges - professional and personal hurdles that need to be cleared on the way - but why not embrace those instead of shying away from them? More and more players are adopting that mindset. Taking that into account, and as we are forever told that travel broadens the mind, GOAL will be helping to tell the story of some of the intrepid explorers that have broken down barriers and found themselves in a position to impart both sporting and holidaying wisdom. Next up is Ollie Bassett, a man who has taken the scenic route from Leicestershire in the East Midlands to the vibrant Canadian city of Toronto… Scouted at a young age Aston Villa started Bassett's development process “I started kicking a ball when I was extremely young, probably three or four. Then I joined my local team that my dad used to coach and manage, with my dad's best friend. They would coach together, so I played for them. When I was about seven or eight, we had a tournament - like a summer event - and there were scouts there. There was a Villa scout. He came over after one of the games and spoke to my dad and his mate about my situation. I joined the academy at Villa when I was seven, but I couldn't properly sign until I was eight because the lowest age group was U8. I trained with them for a little bit and as soon as I signed for the academy, obviously I stopped playing with all my mates. I was at Villa from eight until 16.” Second chance programme A senior debut was taken in with Yeovil “Southampton was kind of a weird story about how it happened. I left Villa when they decided on the scholarships - I didn't get offered one. Then I went to, it wasn't Southampton's actual academy, they call it a second chance programme. They were based down in Bath, and alongside that I was doing college. That was meant to be a two-year programme, like two years for your scholarship. The whole purpose of that programme was to promote players into the Southampton academy. But Southampton at the time thought they weren’t generating enough players into their full academy, so they knocked it on the head. That was meant to be two years, but they knocked it on the head after a year. We were like, ‘well, we've signed a two-year deal, what are we going to do for the second year?’ “It just happened that at the t

item.title: “Hasn’t really recovered”: Peter Schmeichel pinpoints where it has all gone wrong for Senne Lammens at Man United
item.description: “Hasn’t really recovered”: Peter Schmeichel pinpoints where it has all gone wrong for Senne Lammens at Man United Manchester United goalkeeper Senne Lammens had a disastrous evening for the club in their 2-2 draw with Sporting CP. Story of the match The Red Devils made another poor start in Europe, conceding the first goal for the fourth European match in a row. Lammens had actually been the hero moments earlier when he had managed to save Luis Suarez’s penalty but was the villain of the piece just seconds later. The Belgian came charging out of his goal and brought down the Sporting attacker, giving the referee an easy call to make. United then recovered in the second half and fought their way back to a 2-1 lead thanks to two goals from former Sporting hero Bruno Fernandes. Mauricio Pochettino’s side looked like they were destined to hold on and win just their fourth match of the season but they once again got in their own way. Lammens, who was so reliable last year, once again managed to ruin the night when he dropped a cross under very little pressure and Suarez tucked away the rebound in acrobatic style. Peter Schmeichel’s take The Champions League-winning goalkeeper who played for both clubs suggested he was worried that Lammens has not recovered from his disastrous cameo from the bench which cost Belgium in their World Cup defeat to Spain in the summer. Speaking to CBS Sports (via The Sun ), he explained that he doesn’t think taking Lammens out of the team would have any real benefit. He explained, “yeah, I don’t know when that point is. Pochettino has come in, he’s brought his own staff, that means he’s got a new goalkeeping coach. Maybe that is something that can change it for him.” The Dane continued to state, “in the World Cup he came on against Spain and made a mistake. Merino scored and they got knocked out and I feel like he’s lost confidence from that mistake, hasn’t really recovered. As a goalkeeper, when you’re not on your best form you need your defenders in front of you to help you out and they haven’t been able to do that and that just makes it so much worse and today was not a great day for him.” Lammens will likely have a chance to make amends when United welcome Brentford to Old Trafford on Saturday afternoon in Pochettino’s Old Trafford debut. item.title: Texas Faces Its Biggest Test Yet as Undefeated Showdown Looms Against Georgetown
item.description: Nov 17, 2026; New York, New York, USA; Arkansas Razorbacks head coach John Calipari at Madison Square Garden. Mandatory Credit: Wendell Cruz-Imagn Images SAN DIEGO — Thanksgiving Day will feature a matchup between two teams looking to protect perfect records. The No. 7 Texas Longhorns (6-0) will face the Georgetown Hoyas (6-0) on Thursday in the opening round of the Rady Children’s Invitational. Tipoff is scheduled for 2:30 p.m. ET at Jenny Craig Pavilion in San Diego. Both programs have opened the season without a loss. However, Thursday presents a significant early test for each side. The game will air nationally on FS1. The winner advances to Friday’s championship game against either UCLA or Saint Mary’s. Texas Has Been Rolling Through Its Schedule Texas enters the tournament ranked No. 7 in the AP Top 25 and No. 5 in the coaches poll. The Longhorns have scored at least 92 points in five of their six victories. Their latest performance was a 97-61 win over Southern Indiana. Junior center Matas Vokietaitis continues to lead the way. He averages 20.7 points and 8.8 rebounds per game. Vokietaitis recorded 20 points and 10 rebounds in the latest victory. He also leads a Texas lineup featuring five players averaging double figures. Head coach Sean Miller has seen his team establish itself offensively. Texas is averaging 94 points per game through six contests. The Longhorns also secured a notable neutral-site victory over Baylor earlier this season. That experience could prove valuable against Georgetown. Georgetown Has Plenty of Firepower, Too The Hoyas haven’t taken long to make their presence felt this season. Georgetown (6-0) is averaging 83.7 points per game while shooting 50% from the field. The program has already picked up a road victory over Clemson. Senior center Vince Iwuchukwu has been a major difference-maker. He averages 20.8 points and 9.2 rebounds per game. Iwuchukwu is coming off a dominant performance against Coppin State. He finished with a career-high 29 points and 10 rebounds while making all 11 of his field-goal attempts. Guard Jaland Lowe adds another dimension to the offense. He averages 16.3 points and 7.3 assists per game. The Hoyas also have experience against quality competition. Their 86-74 victory over Maryland and road win at Clemson stand out. History Gives Georgetown Another Reason for Confidence Thursday’s matchup will mark the fourth meeting between the programs. Georgetown currently holds a 2-1 advantage in the all-time series. The Hoyas won the most recent meeting, defeating then-No. 22 Texas 82-66 in November 2019. Georgetown head coach Ed Cooley also enters the matchup with a 2-0 record against Texas. Miller, meanwhile, will look to even the series. Both teams have plenty to prove as the tournament begins. Texas has the higher ranking, but Georgetown has already shown it can compete against quality opponents. item.title: What's gone so wrong at Man City? Enzo Maresca's muddled team in danger of complete collapse
item.description: What's going wrong for City_.jpg - Getty/GOAL The confidence-depleted Citizens' miserable recent run continued in Europe this week, and the manager must find solutions for their malaise quickly Enzo Maresca looked like the true heir to Pep Guardiola after the first month of the 2026-27 campaign. Manchester City opened with eight successive wins, including a pair of particularly impressive triumphs away at Manchester United and Liverpool, and had the swagger of genuine contenders, despite the cloud of a guilty verdict in their much-debated Premier League financial case hanging over the club. Continuing with the same slick brand of football Guardiola always championed at the Etihad Stadium, it appeared that Maresca was building something special after a significant squad overhaul in the summer. Unfortunately for City fans, though, the magic has worn off quicker than they ever would have imagined. City have only won one of their last seven games in all competitions, narrowly beating RB Leipzig 3-2 in Germany, while they only progressed to the Carabao Cup quarter-finals after edging Brighton on penalties, having played out a 2-2 draw in normal time. In the Premier League, Maresca's men were humbled by Aston Villa, Brighton and Nottingham Forest before being held to a 1-1 draw at home by struggling Fulham, which left them six points adrift of leaders Arsenal. There was a big opportunity for an uplift on Tuesday as City hosted a Napoli team in freefall under Massimiliano Allegri, but they blew it, ultimately scraping a 2-2 draw that damaged their hopes of automatic qualification for the Champions League last-16. Next up, it's the small matter of a trip to the Emirates Stadium, where Arsenal will be looking to take a massive step towards defending their title. It's shaping up to be a complete mismatch, because City are a mess right now. Their season is in danger of unravelling heading into the festive period unless Maresca can bring back a sense of cohesion. But what exactly has gone so wrong? 'Easy to play through' Napoli ruthlessly capitalised on City's defensive fragility at the Etihad, with their attackers afforded far too much time and space in the final third City twice came from behind to rescue a point against Napoli, with Rayan Cherki stepping up as the hero in the 86th minute, gliding past his marker in the box before firing a precise low shot past Vanja Milinkovic-Savic in the opposing net. Teenage midfielder Ayyoub Bouaddi also netted his first goal for the club, but those two moments of brilliance did not paper over the cracks for City's frighteningly fragile backline. Napoli caught the Citizens trying to play out from the back before opening the scoring, with Billy Gilmour then playing in former Manchester United striker Rasmus Hojlund, who evaded March Guehi with a simple change of direction before finishing into the far corner. The second was even more shambolic, as Matteo Politano took Nico O'Reilly out of the game with a superb hooked

item.title: ‘Am I crazy?’ – Bill Simmons thinks the Packers have been ‘screwed’ by NFL referees in 2026
item.description: Photo by Sean M. Haffey/Getty Images Bill Simmons has publicly brought up one of the major concerns he’s observed about how NFL officials have been treating the Green Bay Packers in the 2026 NFL season. The Packers fell to a 26-13 loss to the Los Angeles Rams on November 25 for Wednesday Night Football. While it was hard to overcome Blake Corum’s 200+-yard rushing performance, Packers fans left the game feeling hard-done by the referees once again. It was a pattern that multiple online fans have been bringing up for weeks that became more apparent after the loss to the Rams. It’s gotten to the point where even Bill Simmons feels like it merits a discussion. Bill Simmons questions if Packers are the worst officiated NFL team in 2026 After the Packers loss to the Rams, veteran media personality Bill Simmons shared a message on X, questioning if his eyes telling him that the Packers are consistently getting screwed is real or not. “Have the Packers gotten screwed by more calls than every other team in 2026 or am I crazy?” There is some truth to Simmons assertion, with specific areas of foul-calling seeing an almost historic swing against the Packers. The Packers have been the most penalised team in the NFL when it comes to roughing the passer, with another controversial call in this regard made against the Rams. The nine roughing-the-passer calls against the Packers are the most in the NFL by more than double, with the second-ranked team picking up four roughing-the-passer calls over the season. Not only that, Packers QB Jordan Love has drawn zero roughing flags this season despite being hit frequently by opposing defenders throughout the season. The disproportionate ‘roughing the passer’ calls for and against the Packers have become too much to ignore. The Packers also rank near the bottom for unnecessary roughness and personal fouls this season. Outside of these specific areas, the Packers have not seen any patterns that break the league’s overall average. Teams like the Carolina Panthers and Cleveland Browns rank higher in terms of the absolute most-penalised teams in the NFL, but the debatable nature of what’s happening in Packers games and the lack of proportion in ‘roughing the passer’ is raising more eyebrows. item.title: Blake Corum celebrates birthday by accomplishing feat not seen in over a decade
item.description: Blake Corum spent his 26th birthday handing out punishment instead of opening presents. The Los Angeles Rams running back bulldozed his way through the Green Bay Packers for a career-high 184 rushing yards on 32 carries in Wednesday night’s 26-13 Thanksgiving Eve victory at SoFi Stadium. Not only were Corum’s 32 carries the most by any NFL running back this season, but they were also the most by a Rams running back in more than a decade. Blake Corum now up to 184 yards rushing pic.twitter.com/xOJ3Oa2ejO — NFL (@NFL) November 26, 2026 Todd Gurley was the last Rams running back to eclipse the 30-carry threshold, rushing 30 times for 159 yards on Oct. 11, 2015, ironically against the same Packers franchise. Aaron Rodgers was Green Bay’s starting quarterback in that 24-10 Rams loss. Blake Corum (24) of the Los Angeles Rams runs the ball against the Green Bay Packers during a game at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, Calif., Nov. 25, 2026. Getty Images Former Washington Commanders running back, Jamie Morris, still holds the NFL’s single-game record with 45 carries in a contest against the Cincinnati Bengals in 1988. Perhaps the most remarkable part of Corum’s accomplishment? He’s not even the Rams’ starting running back. That distinction still belongs to Kyren Williams, although the workload suggests the lines between starter and backup are becoming increasingly blurred. During the Rams’ five-game winning streak, Corum has amassed 508 rushing yards on 88 carries compared to Williams’ 71 attempts. He’s also posted consecutive 100-yard rushing performances for the first time in his NFL career. Los Angeles Rams running back Blake Corum (24) celebrates his touchdown with head coach Sean McVay during an NFL game in Inglewood, Calif., Nov. 25, 2026. AP Photo/Gregory Bull “Coach’s big thing this week was that the most physical team’s going to win, and I think we were that. I know we were that,” Corum said. Behind a patchwork offensive line, Corum chipped away at Green Bay’s defense like a lumberjack taking an axe to a tree. Eventually, the tree fell to the ground. “I did know we were going to wear them out at some point,” Corum said. “They were going to get tired, and that’s when you started getting those chunk plays.” Los Angeles Rams running back Blake Corum (24) eludes Green Bay Packers cornerback Brandon Cisse (2) on Wednesday, Nov. 25, 2026, at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, Calif. Jon SooHoo/UPI/Shutterstock The Rams have gone from 2-4 to 7-4, rediscovering their offensive identity in the process. And the guy listed second on the depth chart is increasingly becoming the engine driving it. item.title: Registered Voters Now 100m As INEC Removes 1.6m Invalid Records
item.description: The Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, said it is now managing a verified voter register of over 100 million. INEC ​‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‍⁠​​⁠⁠‌​‌‌​Chairman, Prof. Joash Amupitan, disclosed this in Abuja on Wednesday, during the commission’s meeting with Resident Electoral Commissioners (RECs) from the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory (FCT). The update comes as the Commission said it has selected 17,676 polling units for the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) mock accreditation and result upload exercise slated for Saturday, 28 November 2026, ahead of the general election in January 2027. According to him, the Commission removed over 1.6 million invalid, duplicated and deceased records from its supplementary voters’ register – the removal has now brought the total verified National Register of Voters from earlier 103 million to more than 100 million citizens. The INEC chairman said that the invalid 1.6 million records were taken off the list, following the application of an Automated Biometric Identification System (ABIS) and statutory claims and objection audit. He noted that no fewer than 11 million people were registered across the three phases of the Continuous Voter Registration (CVR) conducted since 2025, while over 10.77 million new registrants were retained. “Beyond hardware and logistics, we must also account for inclusivity and evidentiary clarity. Following three phases of Continuous Voter Registration (CVR) that added over 10.77 million new registrants and an ABIS and statutory claims-and-objections audit that purged over 1.6 million invalid, duplicate, or deceased records, our verified register stands at over 100 million citizens, including 232,658 Persons With Disabilities (PWDs) requiring accessible polling layouts and assistive materials. “This was before we went into claims and objections. When we activated the claim and objection to the display at the registration areas and also through the internet, we received about 311,000 complaints. “We addressed those complaints and we found that about 232,000 of those complaints were found to be genuine and we’ve been able to address those issues,” he said. INEC Chairman Joash Amupitan Amupitan added that further inquiry from INEC showed that there were an additional 113 which the commission discovered on its own on the supplementary register. He noted that beyond the new supplementary list, most of the complaints received online bordered on anomalies in the existing national register compiled between 2011 and 2023. He said that although INEC had previously stood down its broader revalidation exercise until after the elections, the commission resolved to immediately address serious infractions identified on the old register. “So, consequent upon that, the ICT department, working with the Voter Registry, have been able to complete the validation of those that contain duplications only, and those we had some form of stroke registrations. “In other words, those places where
